arithmetic/add/on-both-sides.reason: Arithmetic on both sides of a comparison cannot be solved to a plain column filter; Prisma filters cannot express column arithmetic

arithmetic/divide/field-by-field.reason: A denominator that is a second column leaves the comparison with two field references and no constant to solve against, which a Prisma where-filter cannot express

arithmetic/divide/nested-division-diviso.reason: The prisma adapter refuses this planner shape at its existing lowering boundary: Unsupported operator: div.

arithmetic/modulo/negative-dividend.reason: Prisma filters have no column arithmetic at all, and `mod` is not in the translator's operator set — the same gap the whole arithmetic/divide group hits, reached here through the modulo operator

cast/double/malformed-string.reason: Prisma filters have no cast operator: double() over a string column cannot be expressed, and CEL's whole-string-or-error parse has no filter form.

cast/double/negated-malformed-string.reason: Prisma where filters expose no scalar cast, positional array index, or RE2 expression for this planner shape.

cast/int/malformed-string.reason: Prisma filters have no cast operator: int() over a string column cannot be expressed, and CEL's whole-string-or-error parse has no filter form.

cast/timestamp/malformed-string.reason: timestamp() over createdBy, a String column: a Prisma DateTime filter needs a column mapped with valueType "dateTime", and comparing the ISO string lexically would not reproduce CEL's parse-or-error semantics.

cast/timestamp/negated-malformed-string.reason: Prisma where filters expose no scalar cast, positional array index, or RE2 expression for this planner shape.

collection/all/nested-exists-over-same-c.reason: Same as collection/exists/nested-over-same-collection, reached through all(): the inner some-filter would have to compare its id and name with the enclosing element's, and Prisma field references stay within one model

collection/except/equals-list-literal.reason: The prisma adapter refuses this planner shape at its existing lowering boundary: Second operand of except must be a lambda expression.

collection/exists-one/several-matches.reason: exists_one requires counting matching elements, which Prisma where-filters cannot express; the adapter throws instead of silently degrading to exists

collection/exists/element-contains-outer.reason: Cross-model comparison plus the column-needle LIKE limitation

collection/exists/element-field-to-outer.reason: Prisma field references only work between fields of the same model; comparing an element column with an outer column is cross-model, so the adapter throws

collection/exists/negated-nested-over-sa.reason: Same as collection/exists/nested-over-same-collection under negation: a Prisma relation filter cannot reference the enclosing element's row

collection/exists/nested-over-same-colle.reason: The inner lambda compares its element with the enclosing element of the same relation. A Prisma relation filter (some/every/none) scopes field references to its own model, and a nested filter cannot name the enclosing element's row, so the comparison has no Prisma spelling; the adapter throws, as for collection/exists/element-field-to-outer-field

collection/exists/outer-collection-insid.reason: Embeds a size(...) == 1 count threshold; same limitation as size/greater-than/collection-above-one

collection/index/first-element-of-boolea.reason: A positional read of a boolean list has no Prisma filter form: Prisma's scalar-list filters (has, hasSome, hasEvery, isEmpty, equals) test membership or the whole list, never one position, and exist only where the provider has array columns, which SQLite and MySQL do not. `index` has no case in the translator's operator switch, so the walk throws at the index node itself, before the list is resolved against the mapper or the element's type meets the literal — the same site as collection/index/first-element-of-string-list

collection/index/first-element-of-number.reason: A positional read of a number list has no Prisma filter form: Prisma's scalar-list filters (has, hasSome, hasEvery, isEmpty, equals) test membership or the whole list, never one position, and exist only where the provider has array columns, which SQLite and MySQL do not. `index` has no case in the translator's operator switch, so the walk throws at the index node itself, before the list is resolved against the mapper or the element's type meets the literal — the same site as collection/index/first-element-of-string-list

collection/index/first-element-of-object.reason: List indexing (tags[0].name): a Prisma relation filter (some/every/none) has no positional element access.

collection/index/first-element-of-string.reason: Indexing a scalar list needs a positional read of an array column, which Prisma's filter API cannot express. The refusal arrives one node earlier than collection/index/first-element-of-object-list's, because there is no get-field projection wrapping this index

collection/index/negative-position.reason: Prisma where filters expose no scalar cast, positional array index, or RE2 expression for this planner shape.

collection/map/equals-list-literal.reason: Prisma can feed a map() projection into hasIntersection, which becomes a relation `some` filter, but list EQUALITY needs the whole ordered projection materialised and compared — there is no Prisma filter that compares a relation projection to a literal list

comparison/equals/whole-list-literal.reason: Prisma scalar comparison and membership inputs cannot bind list or map elements; the translator refuses before constructing a filter.

comparison/not-equals/whole-list-literal.reason: Prisma scalar comparison and membership inputs cannot bind list or map elements; the translator refuses before constructing a filter.

hierarchy/descendent-of/bracket-in-path.reason: Hierarchy prefixes containing [ cannot be matched literally: Prisma emits LIKE without an ESCAPE clause, and [ opens a character class on SQL Server even when one is declared

hierarchy/descendent-of/empty-delimiter.reason: Cerbos splits a path on an empty delimiter into one segment per character, so the relation is a strict string-prefix test; the adapter lowers descendentOf as `startsWith(prefix + delimiter)`, which with an empty delimiter also matches the path itself (a2, never its own descendant). The empty delimiter is refused when the hierarchy operand is parsed, before that filter is built

hierarchy/descendent-of/like-metacharact.reason: Hierarchy descendant prefixes require literal LIKE matching, but Prisma string filters cannot escape % or _; the adapter throws instead of treating them as wildcards

hierarchy/overlaps/like-metacharacters-i.reason: The inclusive overlap union ends in a descendant prefix LIKE on '50%:a_b:'; Prisma emits LIKE without an ESCAPE clause, so % and _ in that prefix stay wildcards and would wrongly admit 50x:a_b:y and 50%:aXb:y — the adapter throws instead

identifier/equals/concatenation.reason: Both operands carry a column: a_optional_string is compared against a concatenation of a constant with the primary key. Prisma's arithmetic solving inverts the constant off the VALUE side to reach a plain column filter, which requires the other side to be a value; a concatenation involving a second column has no Prisma filter form

logic/not/deep-mixed-nesting.reason: Two independent limitations sit in this predicate, and the adapter reports the one its walk reaches first: startsWith(aString, '100%') in the left branch hits the same LIKE-metacharacter limitation as string/starts-with/percent-in-needle, before the right branch's cross-model element-vs-outer column comparison (t.name == R.attr.aString) — which collection/exists/element-field-to-outer-field covers on its own — is ever visited

membership/in/field-in-resource-list.reason: Comparing a related element column with an outer scalar column is cross-model, while Prisma field references are same-model only

membership/in/negated-field-in-resource-.reason: Same cross-model correlated comparison limitation as membership/in/field-in-resource-list, under negation

null/in/missing-attribute-in-resource-li.reason: The prisma adapter refuses this planner shape at its existing lowering boundary: Membership between two database attributes is not supported: Prisma cannot compare a related element column with an outer scalar column.

null/in/negated-missing-attribute-in-res.reason: The prisma adapter refuses this planner shape at its existing lowering boundary: Membership between two database attributes is not supported: Prisma cannot compare a related element column with an outer scalar column.

principal/map/membership-in-mapped-list.reason: The prisma adapter refuses this planner shape at its existing lowering boundary: in requires a field member and literal list, or a literal member and field collection.

regex/matches/lucene-reserved-characters.reason: The prisma adapter refuses this planner shape at its existing lowering boundary: Unsupported operator: matches.

size/equals/filtered-collection.reason: The count is taken over filter(tags, ...) rather than a named relation, and a Prisma where-filter can only count a relation it can name; the underlying relation-count limitation is size/greater-than/collection-above-one's, but this operand shape is rejected one step earlier

size/greater-or-equal/fractional-thresho.reason: Same relation-count limitation as relation/size/non-negative-to-one-chain, reached through a fractional threshold: >= 1.5 rounds up to >= 2, and none/some express only emptiness

size/greater-than/collection-above-one.reason: Prisma where-filters cannot express relation-count thresholds (only empty/non-empty via none/some)

size/less-or-equal/fractional-threshold-.reason: Same relation-count limitation as size/greater-or-equal/fractional-threshold-on-relation under the opposite ordering: <= 1.5 rounds down to <= 1, still an arbitrary count threshold none/some cannot express

string/contains/field-to-field.reason: A column-valued needle would need per-row LIKE escaping, which Prisma filters cannot express; the adapter throws

string/contains/negated-field-to-field.reason: The needle is a COLUMN, so its LIKE metacharacters would have to be escaped per row. Prisma's filters cannot do that, and the negation reaches the same refusal as the positive string/contains/field-to-field — the rejection is decided by the column needle before three-valued logic under the NOT is ever considered

string/ends-with/backslash-in-needle.reason: A backslash is a LIKE metacharacter on some providers and not others, so the same needle cannot mean the same thing on all of them: SQLite's LIKE has no escape character and matches a backslash literally, while PostgreSQL and MySQL treat it as the DEFAULT escape character with no ESCAPE clause present. endsWith('\\') is then a pattern ending in an escape character, which PostgreSQL rejects outright (SQLSTATE 22025), and a backslash anywhere inside a needle silently escapes the next character so contains('a\\b') would match 'ab' — a row the PDP denies. Prisma emits no ESCAPE clause and cannot escape the backslash, so the adapter throws instead of filtering differently per provider

string/ends-with/field-to-field.reason: Same column-needle LIKE limitation as string/contains/field-to-field

string/starts-with/concatenated-literal-.reason: The folded needle is '100%', hitting the same LIKE-wildcard limitation as string/starts-with/percent-in-needle

string/starts-with/field-to-field.reason: Same column-needle LIKE limitation as string/contains/field-to-field

string/starts-with/negated-field-to-fiel.reason: Same column-valued needle as string/contains/negated-field-to-field: escaping per row is what Prisma cannot express, and the negation never gets far enough for the NULL-needle question to arise

string/starts-with/percent-in-needle.reason: Prisma emits LIKE without an ESCAPE clause and does not escape wildcards, so a needle containing % or _ cannot be matched literally; the adapter throws instead of filtering wrong

timestamp/equals/field-to-field-without-.reason: Prisma DateTime values retain instants but discard RFC-3339 lexical spelling; raw field equality cannot reproduce CEL string equality, so both operands require timestamp wrappers.

type-mismatch/equals/boolean-list-elemen.reason: Same missing positional read as collection/index/first-element-of-boolean-list, and the throw lands before the cross-type question this probe asks can arise: the index node is refused before its boolean element meets the number literal, so neither CEL's heterogeneous equality nor a store that reads a JSON true as 1 is ever consulted. The throw propagates out of the `or`, so the aNumber == 5 branch, which the adapter translates on its own, is not emitted either

type-mismatch/equals/number-list-element.reason: Same missing positional read as collection/index/first-element-of-number-list, and the throw lands before the cross-type question this probe asks can arise: the index node is refused before its number element meets the boolean literal, so neither CEL's heterogeneous equality nor a store that reads a JSON true as 1 is ever consulted. The throw propagates out of the `or`, so the aNumber == 5 branch, which the adapter translates on its own, is not emitted either

type-mismatch/less-than/negated-nan-agai.reason: The finite ternary branch compares a numeric value with a mapped string field; Prisma scalar filters cannot encode the CEL type-error result required for that branch and the adapter rejects the mismatched operand type.
